facts: Direct CAO entry to programmes like BSc Paramedic Studies at UL or UCC

Typical entry needs 6 Leaving Cert subjects including Maths, English, and Irish or another language, plus a Lab Science subject (Biology, Physics, Chemistry, Physics & Chemistry, or Agricultural Science) at O6/H7 — some programmes ask H4 in the lab science and H5 in one other subject

Year 1 of most programmes covers the curriculum for PHECC's National Qualification in Emergency Medical Technology (NQEMT); registering with PHECC (Pre-Hospital Emergency Care Council) is required to practise
CAO points weren't independently confirmed in this draft — verify the current points requirement at cao.ie

facts: Direct CAO entry, e.g. TU837 Quantity Surveying & Construction Economics at TU Dublin
Typical entry needs 6 subjects at O6/H7, 4 of those at H5, with Maths and English (or Irish) at O6/H7; a QQI-FET applicant route also exists, capped at 390 points
Real starting pay: roughly 35,000-45,000 euro entry-level, rising toward 70,000 euro within 5-8 years, with average around 59,000 euro overall
Senior QS pay in Dublin reported around 75,000-95,000 euro, somewhat lower outside Dublin
CAO points vary by year and college — verify the current figure at cao.ie before advising a student
Direct CAO entry to BSc Physiotherapy, e.g. DN420 at UCD
Highly competitive course; exact current CAO points weren't independently confirmed in this draft — verify at cao.ie
Real starting pay: entry-level (under 1 year) physiotherapist averages around 34,194 euro total compensation, rising to around 39,624 euro at 1-4 years experience
Often cited as offering strong salary and job security relative to the points needed to get in, compared to some other CAO courses
No CAO points needed: minimum is Grade D in five Junior Cert subjects (or equivalent), age 16+; employers can set extra requirements, and a preparatory course exists for candidates below the minimum
Must be hired by a SOLAS-approved employer first, then registered as an apprentice, same as other craft apprenticeships
7 phases total: 3 off-the-job (in a training centre) and 4 on-the-job (with the employer)
Apprentice pay rises by phase: roughly 274 euro/week (Phase 2) up to roughly 740 euro/week gross by 4th year
Direct CAO entry to BSc Veterinary Nursing at colleges including DkIT, TUS, ATU, and UCD
Typical entry needs 6 subjects, H5 in two of them, O6/H7 in the remaining four including Maths and a language; a lab science subject is also required, at grades that vary slightly by college
Heavy demand year on year, with CAO points recently in the region of 400-430 — always verify the current figure at cao.ie
Alternative entry route: a QQI Level 5 award in any discipline can be used to compete for a place instead of Leaving Cert points

branches.summary: QQI / on-the-job route (not a formal SOLAS apprenticeship)
facts: No SOLAS apprenticeship scheme was found for this role — the real route is QQI-based: a QQI Level 5 Pharmacy Assistant award (or 2+ years full-time pharmacy dispensary experience) as a foundation, then a part-time Pharmacy Technician programme such as TU654 at TU Dublin
Requires working in a pharmacy for a minimum of 20 hours a week for the duration of the course
Programme takes roughly 2 years, combining part-time academic study with practical placement
No CAO points or full-time college attendance needed — it's a trainee/earn-while-you-learn route into the qualification
Real pay: starting salary around 23,157 euro gross/year, average around 29,914 euro gross/year (about 14.38 euro/hour)
sources: tudublin.ie TU654 Pharmacy Technician Studies course page
